stops.note: Pliny the Elder devotes a whole book of his Natural History (Book 14) to vines and the wines of the Roman world
Germanic tribes bought Roman wine across the Rhine and Danube frontiers; the same loan gives German Wein and Gothic wein
Beowulf describes wine poured from 'wondrous vessels' at the feast in the hall of Heorot
Eleanor of Aquitaine's marriage to Henry II in 1152 tied Bordeaux to the English crown, and its 'claret' became England's everyday wine

current_meaning: an alcoholic drink made from fermented grape juice
